# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 2B.2 evidence note

I ran a bounded search pass with multiple query formulations. Best-supported conclusion: **no reliable 2024 evidence that Sharif initiated or expanded a war of choice, annexation campaign, covert destabilization, or proxy conflict beyond defensive necessity**. The strongest contrary material is coercive rhetoric around India/Kashmir, but it is rhetoric rather than a documented war policy.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Peace in South Asia depends on settlement of Kashmir dispute: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-21 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/21-09-2024/peace-in-south-asia-depends-on-settlement-of-kashmir-dispute-pm | Sharif said Pakistan believes in peace and stability through dialogue and that lasting regional peace depends on a peaceful Kashmir settlement. This supports a reading that he preferred diplomacy over coercive expansion. | 2B.2; also 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM urges AJK leadership to resolve issues through dialogue | Radio Pakistan | 2024-05-12 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/12-05-2024/pm-shehbaz-urges-ajk-govt-political-leadership-to-resolve-issues-through-dialogue | During unrest in Azad Kashmir, Sharif told party and local leaders to negotiate with the action committee and resolve the dispute peacefully. This is direct evidence against choosing coercion when a peaceful channel existed. | 2B.2; also 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM urges UN to take action against Israel’s genocidal acts | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-26 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/26-09-2024/pm-urges-un-to-take-action-against-israels-genocidal-acts | In his UNGA speech, Sharif urged confidence-building measures to prevent war between major powers and reduce tensions. That is de-escalatory, not war-expanding, behavior. | 2B.2; also 2B.1, 1B.8 |
| Mixed / negative-adjacent | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | Sharif again called for dialogue on Kashmir, but the same speech also warned Pakistan would respond “most decisively” to Indian aggression and described India’s war doctrine in nuclearized terms. This is the clearest counterevidence, though still rhetorical rather than a war of choice. | 2B.2; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.8, 1B.10 |
| Mixed / negative-adjacent | Pakistan’s stance on Palestine, J&K presented before the world: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-28 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/28-09-2024/pakistans-stance-on-palestine-kashmir-presented-before-the-world-pm | After UNGA, Sharif said he forcefully presented Pakistan’s positions and emphasized strong response language. This reinforces that he paired diplomacy with coercive signaling, but it still does not show a new war, annexation, or proxy escalation. | 2B.2; also 1B.2, 1B.8 |

## Synthesis

- Best-supported reading: **Sharif did not pursue wars of choice, annexation, or proxy conflict in the 2024 material I found**.
- He **did** use hard-edged rhetoric on Kashmir and India, which is the main negative signal.
- I found **no credible 2024 evidence** of a new cross-border offensive campaign, covert destabilization program, or proxy escalation beyond defensive necessity.
- Confidence should remain **moderate-low** because the evidence is mostly public rhetoric and peace-oriented statements, not a full operational record.
